annotationRationale: Parallel-line relations organize the exhaustive cases. Two-point uniqueness controls shared intersections, and the combination formula counts line pairs when all intersections are distinct.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution's classification by concurrence and parallelism. Clarified why pair intersections are distinct when no three lines concur and why repeated values of N are summed only once.

review.mathCheck: Without triple concurrence, parallel-class sizes give N=0,3,4,5,6. Triple concurrence adds only 3 or 4, and quadruple concurrence gives 1. Thus the attainable values are exactly 0,1,3,4,5,6, whose sum is 19, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official #14's first case analysis on p.7. The resulting values also match the official example figures on pp.7-8.
review.annotationCheck: The cases are exhaustive, include the all-parallel arrangement, and establish realizability. Distinct intersections and repeated values are handled correctly. The explanation is reconstructible at AMC 12 level.
